# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 40 FAREWELL TO THE HOUSE OF DREAMS

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Captain Saul was interred within the small graveyard above the harbor, extremely close to the place where the wee white lady rested. A highly costly and remarkably hideous “monument” was erected by his relatives—a memorial that he would have subtly mocked had he observed it while alive. Nevertheless, his true memorial existed within the hearts of the people who knew him, as well as in the book destined to endure for generations.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0000 }

Lorna grieved because Captain Saul had passed away before witnessing how remarkably well it had succeeded.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0001 }

“He would have taken such joy in the reviews, as nearly every one is so warm. And seeing his life's work at the top of the best-seller lists—oh, Nell, if only he had survived long enough to witness it!”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0002 }

Yet Nell possessed greater wisdom, even though she was grieving.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0003 }

“Lorna, it was the actual book he treasured—not any opinions about it—and it belonged to him. Every page had been read by him. A time of immense joy must have been that final evening for him—followed by the swift, effortless passing he had desired come the day. For Adrian and for you, I am happy about the book being so successful—yet Captain Saul was content—I KNOW.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0004 }

The beacon on the point continued its evening watch; a temporary tender had been dispatched to the Point, pending the moment a supreme authority might determine which among numerous hopefuls was most suitable for the position—or possessed the greatest influence. The First Mate resided at the small cottage, adored by Nell and Hugh and Lorna, and endured by a Tabitha who held little affection for felines.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0005 }

“I am able to tolerate him on account of Captain Saul, Mrs. Doctor, dear, because the old man was to my liking. And I shall ensure he receives food and drink, along with all the mice caught by the traps. However, do not request anything beyond that from me, Mrs. Doctor, dear. Cats are cats, and you may take my word that they will not ever be any different. Furthermore, Mrs. Doctor, dear, do at least prevent him from approaching the blessed wee man. Imagine the horror if he were to draw out the darling’s breath.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0006 }

“A CAT-astrophe would be a suitable name for that,” Hugh remarked.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0007 }

“Oh, you might chuckle, doctor, dear, yet it wouldn’t be a matter for laughter.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0008 }

“It is merely an ancient wives’ tale, Tabitha, that cats draw the breath from infants,” Hugh remarked.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0009 }

“Oh, well, doctor, dear, it could be a superstition or it could not. I only know that it took place. The cat belonging to the wife of my sister’s husband’s nephew sucked the breath of their baby, and when it was discovered, the poor innocent was nearly dead. And, Mrs. Doctor, dear, whether it is a superstition or not, I shall strike that yellow beast with the poker if I catch him hiding close to our baby.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0010 }

The green house served as a comfortable and peaceful home for Mr. and Mrs. Ambrose Kerr. Because her wedding to Adrian was set for Christmas, Lorna kept herself occupied with sewing. Considering Lorna's upcoming departure, Nell pondered what her own future held.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0011 }

“Things are constantly changing. Exactly when everything becomes truly wonderful, a shift occurs,” she uttered, sighing.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0012 }

“Up at the Glen, the old Varley place is to be sold,” Hugh remarked, without any particular prompt.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0013 }

“Is that so?” Nell asked with an air of indifference.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0014 }

“Indeed. Since Mr. Varley has passed away, Mrs. Varley desires to relocate to Vancouver to reside with her children. Her asking price will be low, because selling such a large property in a tiny village like the Glen will prove rather difficult.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0015 }

“Indeed, the location is quite lovely, which makes it probable that someone will buy it,” Nell remarked inattentively, debating if she ought to use feather-stitch or hemstitch on young Kit’s "short" frocks. His transition to shorter clothes was scheduled for the following week, a prospect that made Nell feel on the verge of tears.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0016 }

“What if we purchase it, Nell?” Hugh asked softly.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0017 }

Releasing her needlework, Nell gazed intently at him.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0018 }

“Are you not being serious, Hugh?”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0019 }

“Truly I am, darling.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0020 }

“And abandon this precious place—our home of dreams?” Nell asked with disbelief. “Oh, Hugh, it’s—it’s impossible to imagine!”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0021 }

“Hear me out with patience, my love. I understand precisely your feelings regarding this. My own feelings are identical. However, the necessity of our eventual relocation has always been known to us.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0022 }

“Oh, but not so quickly, Hugh—not right now.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0023 }

“An opportunity like this might not come our way a second time. Should we fail to purchase the Varley place, another buyer will—and no remaining home in the Glen appeals to us, nor is there another truly suitable spot where we could construct one. It is true, as I acknowledge, that this tiny home remains—well, it holds a place that no different house could possibly replace for us, yet you are aware of how isolated it is down in this spot for a medical man. We have experienced the difficulty, even if we have managed as best we could. Furthermore, we are squeezed for space in it at present. Maybe, in several years’ time, once Kit requires his own bedroom, it will prove far too cramped.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0024 }

“Oh, I know—I know,” Nell said, her eyes welling with tears. “I am aware of everything that may be urged against it, yet I love it to such a degree—and this place possesses such beauty.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0025 }

“After Lorna leaves—and Captain Saul is departed as well—you would feel quite isolated in this place. Beautiful as the Varley place is, we would come to cherish it as time passes. You must admit you have constantly held it in high regard, Nell.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0026 }

“Oh, yes, but—but—Hugh, this has all appeared to happen so abruptly. I feel lightheaded. A mere ten minutes ago, the idea of abandoning this beloved location had never entered my mind. I was designing my intentions for it during the spring—my plans for the garden. And should we depart from here, who will take possession of it? Being as remote as it IS, some impoverished, lazy, itinerant family will probably lease it—and swarm through it—and oh, that would amount to a desecration. It would cause me immense pain.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0027 }

“I am aware. However, Nell-girl, we must not let such matters compromise our own needs. In all crucial respects, the Varley place fits what we require—missing an opportunity like this is simply beyond our means. Consider the spacious lawn boasting those grand ancient trees, as well as the magnificent twelve-acre hardwood grove situated at the back. It would make an incredible area for our children to play! Additionally, it features a wonderful orchard, and that tall brick garden wall with its inset door has always won your admiration—it struck you as being just like something from a story-book. Furthermore, the Varley place offers a vista of the harbor and the dunes that is nearly as impressive as the one we have from this spot.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0028 }

“The lighthouse star is not visible from there.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0029 }

“Indeed, it is visible out of the attic window. Nell-girl, that is one more benefit—large garrets are a favorite of yours.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0030 }

“In the garden, no brook exists.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0031 }

“Indeed, no, yet a stream flows amidst the maple trees and leads to the Glen pond. Furthermore, that very pond lies quite near. It will be easy for you to imagine that your personal Lake of Glassy Waters is yours once more.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0032 }

“Well, Hugh, refrain from discussing it any further at this moment. Allow me a bit of time to consider it—to become accustomed to the notion.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0033 }

“Very well. Naturally, there is no major rush. However—if we choose to purchase, settling in and moving prior to winter would be ideal.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0034 }

Hugh departed, and Nell stowed Little Kit’s short dresses with shaking hands. Sewing any more that day was impossible for her. Her eyes wet with tears, she roamed through the small realm where she had ruled as such a joyful queen. The Varley place possessed every quality Hugh asserted. Its grounds were lovely, and the dwelling was sufficiently old to possess dignity, repose, and traditions, yet modern enough to remain cozy and up-to-date. Nell had constantly admired it; however, admiration does not equal love, and her affection for this home of dreams was immense. She loved EVERYTHING regarding it—the garden she had cared for, which a great number of women had cared for prior to her—the shimmer and glisten of the small brook sliding so playfully through the corner—the gate set among the creaking fir trees—the aged red sandstone step—the majestic Lombardies—the pair of small, unusual glass cupboards above the hearth in the living-room—the lopsided pantry door inside the kitchen—the pair of amusing dormer windows on the upper floor—the small turn in the stairs—indeed, such details formed a portion of her being! How was she to abandon them?
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0035 }

And in what manner this small home, hallowed in the past through affection and delight, had been hallowed anew for her via her gladness and grief! Within these walls she had passed her honeymoon; within these walls tiny Joyce had existed for her single fleeting day; within these walls the tenderness of maternity had returned alongside Little Kit; within these walls she had listened to the wonderful melody of her infant’s bubbling chuckles; within these walls cherished companions had lingered beside her hearth. Happiness and sorrow, nativity and mortality, had rendered holy for all time this small home of visions.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0036 }

And now it was time for her to depart from it. Even as she had argued against the notion to Hugh, she was aware of that truth. Their small home had become too small for them. The shift was required because of Hugh’s interests; despite the success of his work, his current location restricted it. Nell understood that the conclusion of their time in this beloved home was approaching, and she had to meet the reality with courage. Yet her heart suffered so greatly!
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0037 }

“Tearing a piece out of my life is what it will be like,” she wept. “And oh, if I might only pray that lovely people would settle here after us—or that nobody at all would live here. Even that would surpass being swamped by a crowd that possesses no understanding of the geography of dreamland, nor any knowledge of the history that has endowed this dwelling with its soul and identity. Furthermore, should that kind of clan move in, this spot will fall apart extremely fast—a historic dwelling deteriorates rapidly when it lacks diligent care. They are going to uproot my garden—and allow the Lombardies to grow untidy—and the fence will start resembling a mouth that lost half its teeth—and leaks will develop in the roof—and plaster will drop—and broken window panes will be stuffed with rags and pillows—and every single thing will grow shabby.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0038 }

Nell’s mind envisioned the future ruin of her beloved small home so intensely that it caused her as much pain as though it were already a completed reality. Dropping onto the steps, she wept lengthily and bitterly. Tabitha discovered her in that spot and asked with great anxiety what was wrong.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0039 }

“Have you fallen out with the doctor, then, Mrs. Doctor, dear? Even if you have, do not be anxious. I am told that such an occurrence is very probable for wedded partners, even though I possess no personal experience of that nature. He will feel regret, and the two of you can quickly reconcile.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0040 }

“No, no, Tabitha, a quarrel hasn’t occurred. It is just that—Hugh intends to purchase the Varley property, which forces us to move to the Glen. And my heart will be broken by it.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0041 }

Nell’s emotions were not shared by Tabitha in the slightest. On the contrary, the likelihood of residing at the Glen delighted her immensely. The solitary situation of her dwelling was her single complaint regarding her life in the small cottage.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0042 }

“Oh, Mrs. Doctor, darling, that will be magnificent. Such a grand, spacious place is the Varley house.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0043 }

“I despise large dwellings,” Nell wept.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0044 }

“Ah, well, once you possess six offspring, your hatred for them will cease,” Tabitha observed in a tranquil manner. “Furthermore, our present dwelling has already become insufficient in size for our needs. With Mrs. Vane staying with us, we lack a guest chamber, and no workspace has ever brought me as much annoyance as that pantry. Whichever direction one pivots, a corner is encountered. In addition, this location is completely isolated from society. Nothing whatsoever exists here aside from the landscape.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0045 }

“It may be out of your world, Tabitha, though it is not out of mine,” Nell said, smiling faintly.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0046 }

“I cannot entirely follow your meaning, Mrs. Doctor, dear, though naturally my education is lacking. However, should Dr. Carrow purchase the Varley property, it will certainly be a sound decision, you can rely on that. Running water is installed there, the pantries and closets are delightful, and I have heard that no other cellar on St. Brendan’s Island compares to it. Indeed, the cellar in this house, Mrs. Doctor, dear, has caused me great sorrow, as you are well aware.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0047 }

“Oh, go away, Tabitha, go away,” Nell said forlornly. “A HOME isn’t made by cellars and pantries and closets. Why don’t you weep with those who weep?”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0048 }

“Well, weeping was never something I was skilled at, Mrs. Doctor, dear. Rather than weep alongside folk, I prefer to get to work and brighten their spirits. Now, avoid crying and ruining those pretty eyes of yours. Having served your purpose, this house is fine enough, yet you are long overdue for a superior one.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0049 }

It appeared that Tabitha held the same perspective as the majority of folk. Only Lorna offered Nell a sympathetic understanding. Upon learning what had happened, Lorna also wept copiously. After that, having wiped away their tears, the pair set to work preparing for the move.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0050 }

“Because we have to leave, let’s leave as quickly as possible and get it done,” expressed miserable Nell with resentful acceptance.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0051 }

“You are aware that the beautiful old home at the Glen will become dear to you once you have resided there for a sufficient time to form precious memories around it,” Lorna remarked. “Companions will visit you there, just as they have visited here—joy will bestow splendour upon it on your behalf. At present, you view it merely as a house—however, time will transform it into a home.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0052 }

The following week, Nell and Lorna wept once more as they put Little Kit into shorter clothes. The tragic feeling stayed with Nell until nightfall, when his long nightgown restored her precious child to her once more.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0053 }

“However, rompers will follow—and after that, trousers—and before long, he will be an adult,” she uttered with a sigh.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0054 }

“Well, you would not desire him to remain an infant forever, Mrs. Doctor, dear, would you?” Tabitha remarked. “Bless his innocent heart, he appears far too sweet for anything in his little short dresses, with his dear feet protruding. And consider the reduction in the ironing, Mrs. Doctor, dear.”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0055 }

“Nell, I have just received a missive from Adrian,” Lorna declared, coming in with a glowing countenance. “And, oh! Such wonderful tidings I have. He informs me in his letter that he intends to purchase this property from the church trustees so we can retain it for our summer holidays. Nell, does this not make you happy?”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0056 }

“Oh, Lorna, saying I am 'glad' does not even begin to describe it! It appears nearly too wonderful to be real. My distress will be far less now that I am aware this cherished place is not going to be profaned by a horde of vandals, nor abandoned to collapse into ruins. Indeed, it is wonderful! It is wonderful!”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0057 }

When Nell awoke on an October morning, she realized she had spent her final night beneath her small house's roof. Regret could not be indulged on so busy a day, and the house stood stripped and bare by the time evening arrived. To bid it goodbye, Nell and Hugh were by themselves inside. Along with the final load of furniture, Lorna, Tabitha, and Little Kit had departed for the Glen. Through the windows, which lacked curtains, the light of the sunset poured in.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0058 }

“Does not every bit of it appear so full of grief and rebuke?” inquired Nell. “Oh, my longing for home will be so great at the Glen this evening!”
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0059 }

“Nell-girl, we’ve been extremely happy in this place, haven’t we?” asked Hugh, speaking with deep emotion.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0060 }

Nell gasped, incapable of responding. Hugh stood waiting for her by the gate of fir trees, during the time she walked through the residence and bade goodbye to each room. She was departing; yet the aged house would remain in that place, gazing out to sea via its unusual windows. The winds of autumn would circle it dolefully, and the gray rain would strike it and the white mists would arrive from the ocean to envelop it; and the light of the moon would descend upon it and illuminate the aged tracks where the schoolmaster and his bride had strolled. Upon that aged harbor coast the magic of tale would remain; the wind would continue to blow invitingly across the silver sand-dunes; the waves would continue to summon from the red rock-coves.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0061 }

“Yet we shall be no longer here,” Nell remarked while weeping.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0062 }

Upon stepping outside, she shut and locked the door in her wake. Awaiting her with a smile was Hugh. Toward the north, the light from the lighthouse shone brightly. Shadows were already wrapping themselves around the small garden, in which marigolds were the sole remaining blossoms.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0063 }

Nell dropped to her knees and pressed her lips to the threadbare old step that she had walked over when she was a bride.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0064 }

“Farewell, sweet tiny home of visions,” she uttered.
{: #nw-v04-c40-p0065 }
